images.title: The king's stable
images.purpose: Show the square stable with its horses and the count along each side, with the four corner stalls marked, so the student sees that a corner belongs to two sides.
images.composition: A square ring of 12 stalls in the centre, the number 5 written outside each of the four sides, and the corner stalls highlighted.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas. CENTRE: a square stable seen from above, made of exactly 12 equal square stalls forming a ring: 4 stalls across the top row, 4 across the bottom row, 2 stalls in the left column between them and 2 in the right column between them. The middle of the ring is an empty white square with no stall. All stalls have thin dark outlines. The 4 corner stalls (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right) have a pale reddish purple fill and a thicker #CC79A7 outline; the other 8 stalls are white. Each horse is a filled teal #0072B2 dot, drawn small, in a loose cluster inside its stall, never touching the stall edge. Dots per stall: TOP ROW, left to right: 1, 2, 2, 0. BOTTOM ROW, left to right: 0, 2, 3, 0. LEFT COLUMN, top to bottom: 1, 3. RIGHT COLUMN, top to bottom: 2, 3. A stall with 0 is simply empty. OUTSIDE the square, one large number 5 centred along each side: above the top row, below the bottom row, to the left of the left column, to the right of the right column (4 fives in all). A thin line runs from the top left corner stall to the words corner stall, written outside the square at its upper left. Nothing else is drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A corner stall belongs to two sides, so counting along every side counts that corner twice.
images.description: A square stable of 12 stalls with the king's horses as dots, 5 counted along each side, and the four corner stalls marked.
images.context: This is the chapter's own stable picture with the verified counts. Each side adds to 5: top 1 + 2 + 2 + 0, bottom 0 + 2 + 3 + 0, left 1 + 1 + 3 + 0, right 0 + 2 + 3 + 0. The total is 19, not 20, because the one horse in a corner is counted on two sides. The picture deliberately prints no total and no answer, because the book's question about the mistake is asked later. The stable has the same shape as 12 children around a square, 4 on each side.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the horses on one side, then on all four sides, and to say which stalls two sides share. Do not reveal the total here; the video works the idea with 12 children around a square first. Misconception M_CORNER_TWICE.

image_decisions.why: The square stable with its dots is the book's own figure and the only way to see which stalls two sides share.
